name: US recession risk
summary: Sahm recession indicator at 0.00; yield curve +0.35; weekly jobless claims near a one-year low
state: The real-time Sahm rule indicator is 0.00, far from the 0.5 trigger (FRED). The 10y–2y Treasury curve was +0.35 on 6 Nov. Weekly jobless claims were 189,000 in the week to 31 Oct, and their four-week average of 194,750 is the lowest in the past year (FRED).
for_you: A weak US economy tends to affect global trade and jobs in export-linked sectors. Current labour-market readings do not signal that.
why: A US recession drags world trade, earnings and jobs; it is the single biggest swing factor for the global cycle.
drivers: Labour market, consumer spending, credit conditions, rates and fiscal policy.

rubric.alert: Sahm ≥ 0.50, or two consecutive negative GDP quarters, or NBER declares recession.
rubric.watch: Sahm 0.30–0.49, or one negative GDP quarter, or payrolls negative in a release.
rubric.normal: Sahm rule indicator < 0.30 and no negative GDP quarter in the latest two releases.
